exact_identity: For actual pure input frame F with trace 12 and rank<=12, write x=K3(F). The Cauchy bound in 121 reads Tr F^2 >= x^2/3+(12-x)^2/9 = 208/9 + [8/9](x-8)(x+2). Thus x>8 forces Tr F^2>208/9, and 4S+8C<=64/9 gives x<=8 including equality; no derivative or monotonicity argument outside x>=8 is needed.
strict_deficit: If the existing 121 H-class spinflip condition holds and 4S+8C<64/9, then x<8. For one actual rank-three Q, 3-Tr(QT1)=3-Tr(Qrho)-Tr(QF)/4 >= (8-x)/4. All other five-erasure comparison deficits are nonnegative under the same H-class conditions, so at 0<t<1 the original fixed-Q gap is at least t^3(1-t)(8-x)/4>0, reflected by the actual Q map for negative shrink. This repeats the 129 consequence with the factorization made explicit, not a separate state-family theorem.
boundary_equality_conditions: If Tr F^2=208/9 and K3(F)=8, equality in both Cauchy steps forces the top three eigenvalues to be 8/3 and the at-most-nine remaining nonzero eigenvalues all 4/9; since their sum is 4, there must be exactly nine.
